PAYR-1306.meaning: The claim bills a procedure that the preauthorisation for the case never requested.
fix: Claim only the procedures the preauthorisation requested. Reuse its procedure entries instead of rebuilding them.
Keep each item's Claim.item[].sequence as it was in the preauthorisation.
If treatment needed a procedure the preauthorisation did not cover, request an enhancement before discharge. Follow request a preauthorisation enhancement.

PAYR-1307.title: The procedure quantity is not valid
PAYR-1307.meaning: The claim carries a quantity for a procedure that the payer does not accept for the case.
fix: Compare Claim.item[].quantity with the item at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.
Send the quantity of the procedure actually delivered to the patient.
On the LM100 item, send the number of days the patient was admitted.
For a cyclic procedure, stay within the cycles the insurance plan allows. Payment covers only cycles with a biometric capture.

PAYR-1308.title: The procedure is not in the active claim
PAYR-1308.meaning: The update names a procedure that the claim now open for the case does not contain.
fix: Keep the items of the submitted claim when you answer a query. Change what the query asked for, such as supporting documents.
Reuse the original Claim.identifier and each item's sequence.

PAYR-1309.title: The implant is not in the preauthorisation request
PAYR-1309.meaning: The claim bills an implant that the preauthorisation for the case never requested.
fix: Claim only the implants the preauthorisation requested. Reuse its implant entries instead of rebuilding them.
Keep each item's Claim.item[].sequence as it was in the preauthorisation.
If treatment needed an implant the preauthorisation did not cover, request an enhancement before discharge. Follow request a preauthorisation enhancement.

PAYR-1310.title: The implant quantity is not valid
PAYR-1310.meaning: The claim carries a quantity for an implant that the payer does not accept for the case.
fix: Compare Claim.item[].quantity with the item at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.
Send the quantity of the implant actually delivered to the patient.

PAYR-1311.title: The implant is not in the active claim
PAYR-1311.meaning: The update names an implant that the claim now open for the case does not contain.
fix: Keep the items of the submitted claim when you answer a query. Change what the query asked for, such as supporting documents.
Reuse the original Claim.identifier and each item's sequence.

PAYR-1312.title: The investigation is not in the preauthorisation request
PAYR-1312.meaning: The claim bills an investigation that the preauthorisation for the case never requested.
fix: Claim only the investigations the preauthorisation requested. Reuse its investigation entries instead of rebuilding them.
Keep each item's Claim.item[].sequence as it was in the preauthorisation.
If treatment needed an investigation the preauthorisation did not cover, request an enhancement before discharge. Follow request a preauthorisation enhancement.

PAYR-1313.title: The investigation quantity is not valid
PAYR-1313.meaning: The claim carries a quantity for an investigation that the payer does not accept for the case.
fix: Compare Claim.item[].quantity with the item at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.
Send the quantity of the investigation actually delivered to the patient.

PAYR-1314.title: The investigation is not in the active claim
PAYR-1314.meaning: The update names an investigation that the claim now open for the case does not contain.
fix: Keep the items of the submitted claim when you answer a query. Change what the query asked for, such as supporting documents.
Reuse the original Claim.identifier and each item's sequence.

PAYR-1315.title: The procedure was rejected at preauthorisation
PAYR-1315.meaning: The claim bills a procedure that the payer rejected when it decided the preauthorisation.
fix: Remove the rejected item from the claim.
Read the item adjudication in the preauthorisation's ClaimResponse before you build the claim. The adjudication with category status gives each item's decision.
Build claim items from the approved items only.

PAYR-1316.title: The investigation was rejected at preauthorisation
PAYR-1316.meaning: The claim bills an investigation that the payer rejected when it decided the preauthorisation.
fix: Remove the rejected item from the claim.
Read the item adjudication in the preauthorisation's ClaimResponse before you build the claim. The adjudication with category status gives each item's decision.
Build claim items from the approved items only.

PAYR-1317.title: The implant was rejected at preauthorisation
PAYR-1317.meaning: The claim bills an implant that the payer rejected when it decided the preauthorisation.
fix: Remove the rejected item from the claim.
Read the item adjudication in the preauthorisation's ClaimResponse before you build the claim. The adjudication with category status gives each item's decision.
Build claim items from the approved items only.

PAYR-1318.title: The claim has no requested treatment plan
PAYR-1318.meaning: The claim carries no requested treatment plan for the case, so the payer cannot check it.
fix: Include the treatment items in Claim.item, each with its procedure code, category and amounts.
Reuse the procedure entries from the approved preauthorisation.

PAYR-1319.title: The claim has no requested investigation plan
PAYR-1319.meaning: The claim carries no requested investigation plan for the case, so the payer cannot check it.
fix: Include the investigation items the preauthorisation requested, each with its investigation code and amounts.
Reuse the investigation entries from the approved preauthorisation.

PAYR-1320.title: The payer has no details for the requested investigations
PAYR-1320.meaning: The payer's system holds no details for the investigations the claim requests.
fix: Take codes from the current insurance plan for your hospital. Follow request the insurance plan.
Refresh the insurance plan at least weekly, and at once when the policy is renewed or amended.
Outdated tariff versions cause rate mismatches and automatic claim rejection. Record which plan version each claim used.
Check each code against the insurance plan. A code the plan does not list also returns PAYR-1221.

PAYR-1321.title: The workflow id is not valid for this step
PAYR-1321.meaning: The payer could not process the request because the workflow id it carries is not valid.
fix: Set x-hcx-workflow_id to the code for the claim step you are taking. A new claim is 15, Claim Request Initiated.
For a query response and every other step, take the code from workflow codes.
In PMJAY there is no separate discharge workflow. Submit the claim with the Claim Submitted workflow id, not a discharge code.

PAYR-1322.title: The case is not in a state that accepts this request
PAYR-1322.meaning: The payer refused the request because of the current state of the case it names.
fix: For no active case, check that the case number is the identifier of the approved preauthorisation. A closed claim does not reopen.
For an active instance, wait for the payer's response to the first request on /v1/claim/on_submit. Send the next request on the case after it arrives.
Send every request on a case one at a time. Queue the next request in your system until the previous response arrives.

PAYR-1323.title: The beneficiary's wallet balance is too low
PAYR-1323.meaning: The payer refused the claim because the beneficiary does not have enough scheme balance left.
fix: Check the balance with a coverage eligibility check of purpose validation. It returns the used amount, the available balance and the wallet liability.
Keep the claimed amount at or below the available balance.
If the patient must pay the difference, check that patient liability applies at your hospital.

PAYR-1324.title: The discharge stage is not valid
PAYR-1324.meaning: The claim carries a discharge stage that the payer does not accept.
fix: Send one Claim.supportingInfo entry with category DIS and code DTH, DTM, LAMA or DAMA.
Put the stage in valueString, spelled exactly as one of the accepted values.
Send the entry on every claim, surgical or medical.

PAYR-1325.title: The admission date is not valid
PAYR-1325.meaning: The payer read the admission date in the claim but does not accept it for the case.
fix: Carry each date in its own Claim.supportingInfo entry, built as the claim request bundle shows it.
Use the actual admission date and time from the patient's record.
Send the date as a string value or as timing, in the NRCeS date-time format. Use a full date-time with the offset, in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+05:30.

PAYR-1326.title: The discharge date is not valid
PAYR-1326.meaning: The payer read the discharge date in the claim but does not accept it for the case.
fix: Carry each date in its own Claim.supportingInfo entry, built as the claim request bundle shows it.
Use the actual discharge date and time from the patient's record.
Send the date as a string value or as timing, in the NRCeS date-time format. Use a full date-time with the offset, in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+05:30.

PAYR-1327.title: The admission date is in the wrong format
PAYR-1327.meaning: The payer could not read the admission date in the claim because of its format.
fix: Carry each date in its own Claim.supportingInfo entry, built as the claim request bundle shows it.
Send the date as a string value or as timing, in the NRCeS date-time format. Use a full date-time with the offset, in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+05:30.
Use the same offset on every date in the claim.

PAYR-1328.title: The discharge date is in the wrong format
PAYR-1328.meaning: The payer could not read the discharge date in the claim because of its format.
fix: Carry each date in its own Claim.supportingInfo entry, built as the claim request bundle shows it.
Send the date as a string value or as timing, in the NRCeS date-time format. Use a full date-time with the offset, in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+05:30.
Use the same offset on every date in the claim.

PAYR-1329.title: The registration date is not valid
PAYR-1329.meaning: The payer read the registration date in the claim but does not accept it for the case.
fix: Send the registration date in the Claim.supportingInfo entry with category OTH and code EDT.
Use the actual registration date and time from the patient's record.
Send the date as a string value or as timing, in the NRCeS date-time format. Use a full date-time with the offset, in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+05:30.

PAYR-1330.title: The registration date is in the wrong format
PAYR-1330.meaning: The payer could not read the registration date in the claim because of its format.
fix: Send the registration date in the Claim.supportingInfo entry with category OTH and code EDT.
Send the date as a string value or as timing, in the NRCeS date-time format. Use a full date-time with the offset, in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+05:30.
Use the same offset on every date in the claim.

PAYR-1331.title: The receiver is not registered in NHCX
PAYR-1331.meaning: The payer found that the receiver named in the claim is not a registered participant.
fix: Set x-hcx-recipient_code to the processingID from the get policies response.
Check the code is a registered participant code before you send.
The same condition at the exchange returns NHCX-1003.

PAYR-1332.title: The Claim Review Committee request is not valid
PAYR-1332.meaning: The payer refused a request meant for review of a claim decision.
fix: Check whether the CRC has already decided the case. If it has, the decision stands.
Build the request as ask the payer to reprocess a claim describes.

PAYR-1333.title: The claim type is not valid
PAYR-1333.meaning: The claim says in-patient or out-patient in a way the payer does not accept.
fix: Set Claim.type to the care type of the case. For in-patient care, use SNOMED CT 737481003, Inpatient care management.
Keep the claim type the same as in the approved preauthorisation.

PAYR-1334.title: The payer has no configuration for your hospital
PAYR-1334.meaning: The payer's system holds no configuration for the hospital that sent the claim.
fix: Check that x-hcx-sender_code is your own registered participant code.
Check the provider Organization carries the hospital's HFR id as an identifier with type code NPI. It must match the id recorded in NHCX for your participant code.
If both are right, contact the support team with the case number and your x-hcx-correlation_id.

PAYR-1335.title: The implant quantity is not valid
PAYR-1335.meaning: The claim carries an implant quantity that the payer does not accept.
fix: Send the number of implants actually used.
Compare the quantity with the implant at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.

PAYR-1336.title: The implant unit price is not valid
PAYR-1336.meaning: The claim carries an implant unit price that the payer does not accept.
fix: Take the implant price from the current insurance plan for your hospital.
Refresh the insurance plan at least weekly, and at once when the policy is renewed or amended.
Outdated tariff versions cause rate mismatches and automatic claim rejection. Record which plan version each claim used.

PAYR-1337.title: The implant net amount is not valid
PAYR-1337.meaning: The claim carries an implant net amount that the payer does not accept.
fix: Recalculate net from the quantity and unit price you send for the implant.
Take the implant price from the current insurance plan for your hospital.
Amount calculations that do not add up also return PAYR-1017.

PAYR-1338.title: The implant attachment is not valid
PAYR-1338.meaning: The claim carries an implant attachment that the payer does not accept.
fix: Encode the attachment value as Base64.
Give the attachment a name. The name cannot be empty.
Use one of the allowed content types: application/pdf, application/jpg, application/jpeg, application/png or application/fhir+json.
Keep each document under 2 MB. The whole bundle can be 20 MB at most.

PAYR-1339.title: The implant status is not valid
PAYR-1339.meaning: The claim carries an implant status that the payer does not accept.
fix: Compare the status on the implant with the item at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.
Send Requested as the status on a requested item. The payer requires that value on the LM100 item.
The full list of accepted status values is not yet published.

PAYR-1340.title: The investigation status is not valid
PAYR-1340.meaning: The claim carries an investigation status that the payer does not accept.
fix: Compare the status on the investigation with the item at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.
Send Requested as the status on a requested item. The payer requires that value on the LM100 item.
The full list of accepted status values is not yet published.

PAYR-1341.title: The investigation attachment is not valid
PAYR-1341.meaning: The claim carries an investigation attachment that the payer does not accept.
fix: Encode the attachment value as Base64.
Give the attachment a name. The name cannot be empty.
Use one of the allowed content types: application/pdf, application/jpg, application/jpeg, application/png or application/fhir+json.
Keep each document under 2 MB. The whole bundle can be 20 MB at most.

PAYR-1342.title: A case in progress blocks a new reimbursement request
PAYR-1342.meaning: The payer refused a new reimbursement request because an earlier request on the same case is still in progress.
fix: Wait for the payer's response to the earlier request before you send a new one.
Check that x-hcx-workflow_id is the reimbursement code for the step. Take it from workflow codes.
Send the new request with a new x-hcx-correlation_id once the earlier request is finished.

PAYR-1343.title: A reimbursement was already approved for this case
PAYR-1343.meaning: The payer refused a new reimbursement request because it has already approved one for the same case.
fix: Do not resend the reimbursement request for the case.
To dispute the approved amount, raise a reprocess request instead. A reimbursement reprocess uses its own workflow id, R122.
Follow ask the payer to reprocess a claim for the request itself.

PAYR-1344.title: The payer has no details for the requested procedures
PAYR-1344.meaning: The payer's system holds no details for the procedures the claim requests.
fix: Take codes from the current insurance plan for your hospital. Follow request the insurance plan.
Refresh the insurance plan at least weekly, and at once when the policy is renewed or amended.
Outdated tariff versions cause rate mismatches and automatic claim rejection. Record which plan version each claim used.
Check each code against the insurance plan. A code the plan does not list also returns PAYR-1204.

PAYR-1345.title: The procedure status is not valid
PAYR-1345.meaning: The claim carries a procedure status that the payer does not accept.
fix: Compare the status on the procedure with the item at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.
Send Requested as the status on a requested item. The payer requires that value on the LM100 item.
The full list of accepted status values is not yet published.

PAYR-1346.title: The procedure description is not valid
PAYR-1346.meaning: The claim carries a procedure description that the payer does not accept.
fix: Send the procedure description exactly as the insurance plan gives it for that procedure code.
Refresh the insurance plan at least weekly, and at once when the policy is renewed or amended.

PAYR-1347.title: The procedure type is not valid
PAYR-1347.meaning: The claim carries a procedure type that the payer does not accept.
fix: Send the procedure type the insurance plan gives for the procedure code.
Compare the type with the procedure in the approved preauthorisation.

PAYR-1348.title: The procedure factor is not valid
PAYR-1348.meaning: The claim carries a procedure factor that the payer does not accept.
fix: Compare the factor with the procedure at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.
Do not recompute the factor on your side between preauthorisation and claim.

PAYR-1349.title: The procedure quantity is not valid
PAYR-1349.meaning: The claim carries a procedure quantity that the payer does not accept.
fix: Send the quantity actually delivered, compared with the approved preauthorisation.
On the LM100 item, send the number of days the patient was admitted.
For a cyclic procedure, stay within the cycles the insurance plan allows.

PAYR-1350.title: The procedure net amount is not valid
PAYR-1350.meaning: The claim carries a procedure net amount that the payer does not accept.
fix: Take the package cost from the current insurance plan for your hospital.
Recalculate net from the quantity, factor and unitPrice you send.
Amount calculations that do not add up also return PAYR-1017.
Outdated tariff versions cause rate mismatches and automatic claim rejection. Record which plan version each claim used.

PAYR-1351.title: The procedure speciality code is not valid
PAYR-1351.meaning: The claim carries a procedure speciality code that the payer does not accept.
fix: Send the category code of the specific cost of the plan in the insurance plan, for example MG for General Medicine.
Take the procedure and its speciality from the same entry in the insurance plan.
Refresh the insurance plan at least weekly, and at once when the policy is renewed or amended.

PAYR-1352.title: The beneficiary and care plan do not fit this hospital
PAYR-1352.meaning: The beneficiary and care plan in the claim match no rule for handling the case at this hospital.
fix: Use the same beneficiary and care plan details as the approved preauthorisation.
Take the treatment from the insurance plan for your hospital.
Refresh the insurance plan at least weekly, and at once when the policy is renewed or amended.

PAYR-1353.title: The care plan id is not valid
PAYR-1353.meaning: The claim carries a care plan id the payer does not accept.
fix: Use the care plan recorded when the beneficiary was registered.
Keep the care plan id the same as in the approved preauthorisation.

PAYR-1354.title: The claim failed a payer rule
PAYR-1354.meaning: The claim failed one of the payer's rules, and the message does not name the rule.
fix: Recheck each package in the claim against the claim conditions in the insurance plan.
Compare the claim with the approved preauthorisation, item by item.
If you find nothing, contact the support team with the case number and your x-hcx-correlation_id.

PAYR-1355.title: The payer has no details for the requested implants
PAYR-1355.meaning: The payer's system holds no details for the implants the claim requests.
fix: Take codes from the current insurance plan for your hospital. Follow request the insurance plan.
Refresh the insurance plan at least weekly, and at once when the policy is renewed or amended.
Outdated tariff versions cause rate mismatches and automatic claim rejection. Record which plan version each claim used.
Check each code against the insurance plan. A code the plan does not list also returns PAYR-1225.

PAYR-1356.title: The wallet is short and the patient cannot pay the difference
PAYR-1356.meaning: The beneficiary's scheme balance does not cover the amount, and the hospital may not charge the patient the rest.
fix: Check the balance with a coverage eligibility check of purpose validation. It returns the available balance and the wallet liability.
Reduce the claimed amount by the deficit in the message, so it stays within the available balance.

PAYR-1357.title: The admission date is after the discharge date
PAYR-1357.meaning: The claim gives an admission date later than its discharge date.
fix: Correct whichever date is wrong, using the patient's record.
Use the same offset, +05:30, on the admission and discharge dates.
Carry each date in its own Claim.supportingInfo entry, built as the claim request bundle shows it.

PAYR-1358.title: The patient was registered too long after admission
PAYR-1358.meaning: The registration date in the claim is later after admission than the scheme allows.
fix: Check the registration date against the patient's record and correct it if it is wrong.
Check the admission date as well. A wrong admission date moves the window.
Use the same offset, +05:30, on both dates.

PAYR-1359.title: The claim has no billable treatment plan
PAYR-1359.meaning: The treatment plan in the claim has nothing the payer can bill for the case.
fix: Send at least one treatment item with its code, quantity, unitPrice and net.
For a discharge against medical advice before or during surgery, add the LM100 item.

PAYR-1360.title: An item code is not valid
PAYR-1360.meaning: The claim carries an item code the payer does not accept at the named item sequence.
fix: Take each item code from the current insurance plan for your hospital.
Compare the code with the item at the same sequence in the approved preauthorisation.
Refresh the insurance plan at least weekly, and at once when the policy is renewed or amended.

PAYR-1361.title: An item sequence is not valid
PAYR-1361.meaning: The claim carries an item sequence number the payer does not accept.
fix: Keep the sequence each item had in the approved preauthorisation.
Give every item its own sequence number.
Check that careTeamSequence, diagnosisSequence, procedureSequence and informationSequence point at entries in the claim.

PAYR-1362.title: A discharge against medical advice needs the LM100 procedure
PAYR-1362.meaning: The patient left against medical advice before or during surgery, and the claim lacks the special procedure for that case.
fix: Add an item with procedure code LM100 and status Requested.
Set its quantity to the number of days the patient was admitted.
Remove the other preauthorisation items. LM100 is the only procedure accepted, and only the actual stay is payable.
Keep the discharge entry: category DIS, code LAMA or DAMA, and the stage as its value.

PAYR-1363.title: No biometric authentication and no consent questionnaire at discharge
PAYR-1363.meaning: The claim carries neither proof that the patient was present at discharge nor the consent questionnaire that replaces it.
fix: Authenticate the patient by fingerprint or iris or face at discharge. Pass the user token as a header parameter on the claim submission.
If biometric authentication is not possible, send the Authentication Consent Questionnaire response. Take the questionnaire for the policy from the insurance plan.
Add the response as a QuestionnaireResponse in the bundle. Reference it from Claim.supportingInfo with category INF, as the claim request bundle shows.
A cyclic package cannot use the consent form. Biometric authentication is mandatory at its discharge.

PAYR-1364.title: A consent questionnaire answer is empty
PAYR-1364.meaning: The consent questionnaire response in the claim leaves one of its questions unanswered.
fix: Answer every question in the questionnaire. Give the item with the named link id a value.
Take the questions from the insurance plan for the policy, and refresh it when the policy changes.
Authenticate the patient by fingerprint or iris or face at discharge. Pass the user token as a header parameter on the claim submission.

PAYR-1365.title: The standard treatment guideline response is missing
PAYR-1365.meaning: A procedure in the claim needs its treatment guideline questionnaire answered, and the claim does not include the answer.
fix: Take the STG questionnaire for the procedure from the insurance plan.
Send the questionnaire URL from the insurance plan back in the questionnaire response.
Reference the response from Claim.supportingInfo with category STG and the value as a reference.

PAYR-1366.title: The biometric user token is not valid
PAYR-1366.meaning: The token from the patient's biometric authentication is not valid for this claim.
fix: Authenticate the patient again at discharge and send the new token with the claim.
Refresh the token automatically until the transaction cycle completes. If it expires, start a fresh biometric authentication.
For a cyclic procedure's claim, a still-valid refresh token from the last cycle is allowed. A new token is preferred.
If biometric authentication keeps failing, use the Authentication Consent Questionnaire for discharge instead.

PAYR-1367.title: No biometric record for a cycle date
PAYR-1367.meaning: The payer found no biometric authentication of the beneficiary for a date the claim gives for a treatment cycle.
fix: Capture a live biometric authentication at every cycle, with process type Discharge. A refresh token is not allowed for a cycle.
Set each cycle's timingPeriod start and end to its biometric capture times.
Claim only the cycles that have a biometric capture. Payment covers only those.

PAYR-1368.title: Cycle information is missing for some cycles
PAYR-1368.meaning: The claim for a cyclic procedure does not carry information for every cycle it requests.
fix: Send one Claim.supportingInfo entry per cycle, with category CD and code TD.
Give each entry a timingPeriod start and end that match that cycle's biometric capture.
List every cycle entry's sequence in the item's informationSequence.
Set the item quantity to the cycles actually given.

PAYR-1369.title: Two biometric authentications on one date for a cyclic procedure
PAYR-1369.meaning: The claim gives more than one biometric authentication on the same date for a cyclic procedure.
fix: Correct the biometric authentication dates for each cycle, using your capture records.
Space cycles at least 24 hours apart from capture to capture. That also keeps them on different dates.
Disable biometric capture for the procedure for 24 hours after each capture in your system.

PAYR-1370.title: A supporting detail has an invalid start date
PAYR-1370.meaning: An entry in the claim's supporting information carries a start date the payer does not accept.
fix: Send timingPeriod.start as a full date-time with offset, for example 2026-08-05T13:01:33+05:30.
For each cycle of a cyclic procedure, set the start and end to the biometric capture times for that cycle.
Keep the entry's sequence and the item's informationSequence pointing at each other.

PAYR-1401.title: The policy is not allowed for your hospital
PAYR-1401.meaning: The payer will not give your hospital the plan for this policy, and only the technical support team can change that.
fix: Confirm that <policy_code> in the message is the policy you meant to request.
Contact the technical support team. Give them the full message, <policy_code>, your participant code, your HFR id and the x-hcx-correlation_id of the refused request.
After support resolves it, send a new request.

PAYR-1402.title: The payer has no policy with the code you requested
PAYR-1402.meaning: The payer could not find the policy code in your insurance plan request, so it returned no plan.
fix: Compare <policy_code> in the message with the policyNumber value you sent. Look for a typing error, a space or a wrong segment. The sample policy codes are PMJAY/HP/S/G and PMJAY/CH/S/G.
Take the policy code from your coverage eligibility result, not from free text.
If the code is correct, contact the technical support team. Give them the full message and the x-hcx-correlation_id of the refused request.

PAYR-1403.title: The renewal does not belong to the requested policy
PAYR-1403.meaning: The payer knows the policy you asked about but not the renewal you named under it, so it returned no plan.
fix: Compare <renewal_code> and <policy_code> in the message with the values your system sent. Correct whichever is wrong.
If both are correct, contact the technical support team. Give them the full message and the x-hcx-correlation_id of the refused request.

PAYR-1404.title: No treatment is configured for the policy under any speciality
PAYR-1404.meaning: The payer has the policy you asked about but no speciality or treatment set up under it, so there is no plan to return.
fix: Compare <policy_code> in the message with the policyNumber value you sent. Correct it if it is not the policy you meant.
If the policy code is correct, contact the technical support team. The payer has to configure a speciality for the policy. Give them the full message and the x-hcx-correlation_id.

PAYR-1405.title: The payer has no enrolled hospital for your HFR id or sender code
PAYR-1405.meaning: The payer could not find your hospital in its records from the facility registry id or sender code you sent, so it returned no plan.
fix: Compare <hfr_id> in the message with your facility's HFR id. Correct the providerId value if it differs.
Send the HFR id that matches the registry id recorded for your participant in NHCX.
Check that <sender_code> is your own participant code.
If both values are correct, contact the technical support team. Your hospital's enrolment with the payer has to be checked. Give them the full message and the x-hcx-correlation_id.

PAYR-1406.title: An earlier insurance plan request for the same policy is still running
PAYR-1406.meaning: The payer is still working on an earlier plan request from your hospital for the same policy, so wait before asking again.
fix: Do not send another request for the same policy. Each one is refused while the earlier one runs.
Wait 15 to 60 minutes. Watch /v1/insuranceplan/on_request for the answer to the earlier request.
If no answer arrives after 60 minutes, contact the technical support team. Give them the correlation id from the message.

PAYR-1501.title: The surgery date entry carries the wrong kind of value
PAYR-1501.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your preauthorisation or claim because the surgery date entry holds a value that is not a date, a period or text.
fix: Find the supportingInfo entry whose sequence matches the message.
Send the surgery date in that entry as a string in the NRCeS date-time format. Keep category ONS and code PSP.
Replace the value. Do not send an attachment or a reference in this entry.

PAYR-1502.title: The admission date entry carries the wrong kind of value
PAYR-1502.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your preauthorisation or claim because the admission date entry holds a value that is not a date, a period or text.
fix: Find the supportingInfo entry whose sequence matches the message.
Send the admission date in that entry as a string in the NRCeS date-time format. Keep category ONS and code ADDD.
Replace the value. Do not send an attachment or a reference in this entry.

PAYR-1503.title: The death date entry carries the wrong kind of value
PAYR-1503.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your claim because the death date entry holds a value that is not a date, a period or text.
fix: Find the supportingInfo entry whose sequence matches the message.
Send the death date in that entry as a string in the NRCeS date-time format. Keep category ONS and code DTM.
Replace the value. Do not send an attachment or a reference in this entry.

PAYR-1504.title: The case remarks in your query response are not text
PAYR-1504.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your answer to its query because the overall case remarks were not sent as text.
fix: Find the supportingInfo entry whose sequence matches the message.
Put the remarks in that entry as a string, with category NMI and code CQD.
Replace any attachment or reference in this entry with the text itself.

PAYR-1505.title: A questionnaire response is attached under the wrong category or code
PAYR-1505.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your preauthorisation or claim because a questionnaire answer is attached under a category and code it does not accept.
fix: Find the supportingInfo entry whose sequence matches the message.
Set its category and code to the pair for what it attaches, as in the table.
Point its valueReference at a QuestionnaireResponse resource included in the same bundle.

PAYR-1506.title: The newborn's gender is not valid
PAYR-1506.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your newborn case because the child's record has no valid gender.
fix: Find the child Patient resource that the parent's link points to.
Set gender to a code from the value set above.

PAYR-1507.title: The newborn's date of birth is not valid
PAYR-1507.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your newborn case because the child's record has no valid date of birth.
fix: Find the child Patient resource that the parent's link points to.
Set birthDate to the child's date of birth, in the form YYYY-MM-DD.
Check the date is not in the future and is within 6 years of the current date.

PAYR-1508.title: The newborn link does not lead to a Patient resource
PAYR-1508.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your newborn case because the parent's link to the child does not lead to a valid patient record.
fix: Find the reference from the message in your bundle.
Make sure one bundle entry has that reference as its fullUrl, and that its resource is a Patient.
Put the child's details in that resource: gender, date of birth and name.

PAYR-1509.title: The newborn's proof of birth attachment is not valid
PAYR-1509.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your newborn case because the proof of birth document is missing or unusable.
fix: Add or correct the proof of birth entry. Use category DOB and code BCF or DCB.
Encode the document as Base64, give it a name and set an accepted content type.

PAYR-1510.title: A parameter code in your request is not valid
PAYR-1510.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your request because one of its parameter codes is not a code it accepts.
fix: Compare every Task.input type code and system in your request with the table.
Check the other coded values in your bundle against the sample bundles and the NRCeS code systems.
If you cannot find the parameter, contact the NHCX support team. Give them the full message and the x-hcx-correlation_id.

PAYR-1511.title: A parameter value in your request is not valid
PAYR-1511.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your request because one of its parameter values is not a value it accepts.
fix: Check each Task.input value in your request against the table.
Take reference numbers from the payer's earlier responses, not from free text.
If you cannot find the parameter, contact the NHCX support team. Give them the full message and the x-hcx-correlation_id.

PAYR-1512.title: A patient reference does not lead to a Patient resource
PAYR-1512.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your request because a reference to the patient does not lead to a valid patient record.
fix: Search your bundle for the reference in the message.
Make sure one bundle entry has that reference as its fullUrl, and that its resource is a Patient.
Check the reference is spelled the same in both places.
Validate the bundle against the NRCeS profiles before you send it.

PAYR-1513.title: A diagnosis is not sent as a coded concept
PAYR-1513.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your request because a diagnosis was not sent as a code with its system.
fix: Send every diagnosis as a diagnosisCodeableConcept with at least one coding:
Check every entry in the list, not only the first. Validate the bundle against the NRCeS profiles before you send it.

PAYR-1514.title: The discharge information entry does not name a discharge stage
PAYR-1514.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your claim because the discharge information entry was not text naming the discharge stage.
fix: Find the supportingInfo entry whose sequence matches the message.
Send the discharge stage in that entry as a string, with category DIS and the code for the discharge.

PAYR-1515.title: An organisation in your bundle has no name
PAYR-1515.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your request because an organisation record in it has no valid name.
fix: Find the Organization resource whose fullUrl matches the reference in the message.
Set its name to the organisation's name. Do not send an empty string.
Check every other Organization resource in the bundle, for the provider and the payer alike.
Validate the bundle against the NRCeS profiles before you send it.

PAYR-1516.title: The payer cannot match your error response to any message
PAYR-1516.meaning: The scheme payer refused an error response from your system because its identifiers match no message the payer knows about.
fix: Take the identifiers for your error response from the message you are answering. Do not generate a fresh correlation id for a response.
Set x-hcx-sender_code to your own participant code. Set x-hcx-recipient_code to the sender of the message you answer.
Follow the identifier rules for responses in Correlation id, API call id and workflow id.
If the identifiers match and the code comes back, contact the NHCX support team. Give them the three values from the message.

PAYR-1517.title: Your error was sent encrypted instead of as a protocol response
PAYR-1517.meaning: The scheme payer refused an error from your system because it arrived in the encrypted structure instead of the protocol response structure.
fix: Send the error as a ProtocolResponse. Its headers travel in clear, with the error in x-hcx-error_details:

x-hcx-entity-type is one of coverageeligibility, payment, insuranceplan, task, claim or preauth. x-hcx-ben-abha-id carries the beneficiary's ABHA number. Set the identifiers as Correlation id, API call id and workflow id describes.

PAYR-1518.title: Your Task resource carries no input parameters
PAYR-1518.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your task request because the task carries none of the inputs it needs.
fix: Add the inputs your request needs, from the table.
Give each input a type coding, with a system and a code, and a value. An input with no type returns PAYR-1519.

PAYR-1519.title: A Task input parameter has no type
PAYR-1519.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your task request because at least one of the task's inputs does not say what kind of input it is.
fix: Check every Task.input entry, not only the first.
Give each one a type.coding with a system and a code from the table.
Keep the value next to its type, as valueString or valueReference.

PAYR-1520.title: The communication reference does not lead to a Communication resource
PAYR-1520.meaning: The scheme payer rejected your answer to its request for information because the reference to your communication does not lead to a communication record.
fix: Search your bundle for the reference in the message.
Make sure one bundle entry has that reference as its fullUrl, and that its resource is a Communication.
Point the include input at that entry:
